overview: Lead is a naturally occurring toxic metal found in the Earth’s crust. Its widespread use has caused extensive environmental contamination, human exposure and significant public health problems globally. Young children are particularly vulnerable to the toxic effects of lead and can suffer permanent adverse health impacts, particularly on the development of the central nervous system.
treatment: identification of the source of lead exposure and termination of exposure
transmission: ingestion of contaminated dust, soil, water or food
pica (compulsive, habitual consumption of non-food items)
prevention: legally binding laws to control the use of lead in paint
